section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Stretch' Concept
section_1.content: Introduce linear transformation as a visual deformation of space. Explain that while most vectors change direction when a matrix is applied, 'Eigenvectors' are the special directions that stay fixed on their original span.
section_1.example: Visualize a grid of rubber bands: Applying a matrix is like stretching the grid. Most arrows rotate, but an eigenvector remains pointing along the same line, just elongated or compressed.

section_2.title: Mathematical Definition: The Eigen-Equation
section_2.content: Define Av = λv. Explain that 'v' (eigenvector) is the direction, and 'λ' (eigenvalue) is the scaling factor. Emphasize that for a non-zero vector to exist, det(A - λI) must equal zero.
section_2.example: If matrix A scales a vector v by 3, λ=3. The equation Av = 3v shows the output is just a scalar multiple of the input.

section_3.title: Visualizing Eigenbasis
section_3.content: Explain that if we have enough linearly independent eigenvectors, they form a 'basis' for the space. In this basis, the transformation matrix becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making complex calculations trivial.
section_3.example: Imagine a 2D plane defined by two eigenvectors. Instead of using x and y coordinates, we describe the world using 'eigen-coordinates', where every movement is just an independent stretch along these two axes.

section_4.title: Real-world Application: Vibration & Stability
section_4.content: Connect the concept to physical systems. Eigenvalues represent natural frequencies of vibration, and eigenvectors represent the 'shape' of those vibrations.
section_4.example: A suspension bridge: Eigenvectors represent the specific shapes the bridge can bend into, and eigenvalues represent the frequencies at which it might collapse due to resonance.

section_5.title: Summary & Quick Check
section_5.content: Recap: Eigenvectors = Directions that don't rotate; Eigenvalues = Scale factors; Eigenbasis = A simplified coordinate system.
section_5.example: A quick visual quiz: Show a transformation animation and ask students to identify the direction that did not rotate (the eigenvector).
